title: Rain intensifies in Kerala, CM directs Idukki, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam collectors to be ready for emergency situation
content: As rain continues unabated in Kerala, Chief Minister V D Satheesan has directed the Collectors of Idukki, Kottayam and Pathanamthitta districts to gear up for any kind of emergency situation. The Chief Minister has entrusted each minister with the responsibility of coordinating rescue operations in a district. C P John (Thiruvananthapuram), P C Vishnunath (Pathanamthitta), Mons Joseph (Kottayam) and Anoop Jacob (Idukki) will camp in respective districts. Revenue Minister will coordinate operations at the state level. V D Satheesan also spoke to the MLAs and assessed the situation. Heavy rain continued to batter large parts of Kerala, particularly the central districts, early on Saturday, triggering landslides, flooding and widespread waterlogging. A red alert has been declared in nine districts. The IMD has predicted extreme rainfall in Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, Kasaragod, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, and Thrissur. Ranni town was completely flooded in the heavy showers. A woman was killed after a landslide triggered by incessant rain buried a house at Adurmala in Kudayathoor, near Thodupuzha, in Idukki district. The deceased was identified as Sumathi, a resident of Mashikkallel House in Ward 7 of Kudayathoor. Her body was recovered around 7 am after an extensive search operation that began in the early hours of Saturday. Her husband, Ravi, and their son, Ratheesh, sustained injuries and were rescued from the debris. The landslide struck around 2 am, completely burying and destroying the family's house. In a second incident, Prabhakaran Nair (72), a native of Vaikom, was killed after a huge mass of earth crashed through the window of the room where he was sleeping at his relative's house, Pournami Nivas, in Kolahalamedu, Vagamon. Prabhakaran, uncle of the house owner Leelamani, had arrived at the house only a day earlier. His room was completely buried under mud and debris, while Leelamani, who was in an adjacent room, escaped unhurt. Fire and Rescue Services personnel, police, and local residents carried out a rescue operation for several hours before recovering the body at around 10.30 am. An earthmover was used to remove part of the house and clear the debris. Vagamon police have initiated further proceedings, and the body will be handed over to the family after the post-mortem examination. Meanwhile, a youth, identified as Joseph Johnny and his mother, Regina Johnny, died in a landslide that occurred at Poonjar around 3.00 am. In Wayanad, a farmer was found dead near a pond on his farmland at Manjoora near Kalpetta on Saturday morning in what is suspected to be a case of electrocution while operating a water pump. The deceased was identified as Mankott Benny, 57, son of Devasya and the late Eliyamma, a native of Manjoora. Benny had left his house early in the morning to switch on a water pump installed near the pond to irrigate his farmland. When he did not return even after a considerable time, his wife, Molly, went in search of him. She found him lying motionless on the ground near the pump house. She immediately alerted neighbours and relatives, who rushed to the spot and shifted Benny to Fathima Hospital, Kalpetta. However, doctors declared him 'brought dead'. Benny is survived by his wife, Molly, and two sons, Albin and Melbin, both of whom are employed in the United Kingdom. In Malappuram, Abdul Muhaini, a three-year-old boy, died after falling into a stream. At Mathayippara in Upputhara, another landslide hit a police jeep. Fortunately, the police personnel had stepped out of the vehicle moments earlier and escaped unhurt. Two minor landslides were also reported at Nellappara in Karinkunnam, though no casualties were reported. In Kottayam district, a landslide occurred near the Mankombu Temple area in Moonnilavu. In Pathanamthitta district, landslides were reported from several hilly areas as heavy rain continued through the night...
